extracted.intended_audience: math olympiad students, coaches, and problem-solvers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or producing high-quality olympiad-style mathematical solutions by recognizing and correctly applying Engel's catalogue of heuristic strategies and related solution-quality criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Invariance Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a quantity preserved under the moves and show it cannot reach the target value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when a process or sequence of moves is involved; judge whether the solver identified a preserved quantity and used it to rule out/guarantee configurations. Check that the invariant is clearly defined and shown to be unchanged by the allowed operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coloring Proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign colors so that a parity or counting argument forces the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the coloring is chosen to expose parity/counting constraints and whether the argument follows cleanly from the coloring; verify that no cases are omitted and that the coloring is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Extremal Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick the maximum/minimum element of a set; the choice forces structural conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for selection of an extremal element and a logical deduction from extremality. Confirm base-case considerations (existence of extremal element) and that the extremal choice leads to the claimed contradiction or construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Box (Pigeonhole) Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Count more objects than boxes; some box has multiple objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the partitioning into boxes is natural and whether counting is rigorous. Check for sharpness and whether stronger pigeonhole conclusions (e.g., quantitative bounds) are properly derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerative Combinatorics
rubrics_metrics.description: Count cleverly with bijections, generating functions, inclusion-exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge correctness and elegance of counting approach, choice of bijection or generating function, and whether edge cases and overcounting/undercounting are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisibility, modular arithmetic, classical congruences, primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess use of congruences, divisibility arguments, and classical lemmas; check rigor in modular reductions, cases, and any appeals to known results (e.g., lifting the exponent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: AM-GM, Cauchy-Schwarz, rearrangement, Jensen, SOS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if an appropriate inequality was chosen and applied correctly, whether equality cases are identified (tightness), and whether the inequality use is the minimal machinery needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Induction Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong induction, downward induction, infinite descent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check base cases, correct inductive hypotheses, and justification of steps (including subtle forms like infinite descent). Watch for omitted base cases or unjustified strengthening of the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Recurrences, telescoping, generating functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate derivation of recurrences, correctness of telescoping sums, and valid use of generating functions; ensure initial conditions and convergence/validity issues are addressed where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Roots, symmetric functions, irreducibility, Vieta.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge correct manipulation of polynomial identities, justification of root-related claims, and proper use of symmetric function properties or irreducibility arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional Equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitution patterns, fixed points, regularity from algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess systematic exploration of substitutions, verification of regularity/continuity assumptions if used, and identification/justification of all solutions (including pathological ones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthetic, coordinate, complex-number, vector, transformational methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate choice of geometric framework (synthetic vs analytic), clarity of construction and diagrams, and whether classical lemmas are correctly applied; prefer structural insight over heavy algebraic computation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Games
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy stealing, pairing, mirror strategies, Sprague-Grundy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check correctness of combinatorial game analysis, validity of strategy-stealing/mirroring arguments, and correct computation or use of Grundy numbers when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Extremal-by-construction, double counting, invariants over more general structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize less-standard or composite strategies; evaluate how they are constructed from basic ideas and whether their application is justified and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the solver identify which of the standard strategies applied?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary evaluative criterion: check whether the solver mapped the problem to an appropriate strategy early and explicitly, rather than stumbling upon calculations without a guiding idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the chosen strategy applied cleanly (no false moves)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for internal logical consistency, no unjustified steps, proper handling of subcases, and avoidance of dead-end manipulations that don't advance the strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum machinery needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer solutions that use the least heavy tools required; penalize overcomplicated approaches when a simpler strategy suffices. 'Economy' includes clarity and concision of argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the argument also handle the general case, not just the stated n?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award solutions that prove broader statements when appropriate or explain why the solution is specialized; check for hidden assumptions that limit generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete case enumeration
rubrics_metrics.description: Are all cases covered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the solution treats every possible case or justifies reductions (e.g., symmetry or monotonicity) that eliminate cases; watch for unjustified WLOG claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound tightness
rubrics_metrics.description: When bounds are involved, are they tight (with equality conditions stated)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require identification of equality/tightness conditions where appropriate and prefer arguments that achieve or explain optimal bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction explicitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence claims are backed by explicit constructions when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether constructive proofs give a clear method and whether non-constructive existence claims are justified; prefer explicit examples or algorithms when they clarify existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repertoire breadth
rubrics_metrics.description: How many of the 14 strategies the student has internalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use breadth as a long-term skill metric: a solver who can draw from a wide range of strategies is stronger; look for demonstrated facility across multiple strategy types in solutions and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern recognition speed
rubrics_metrics.description: How quickly the student maps a problem to its strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contest settings, speed of recognition matters; evaluate whether the solver quickly sees the structural hint that suggests a particular heuristic rather than laboring through blind computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-strategy fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to combine strategies (e.g., extremal + invariance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward elegant combinations where two or more strategies interact; check that the interaction is logically coherent and each part is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to abandon a strategy that isn't working and try another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess metacognitive flexibility: does the solver recognize dead ends and pivot? Partial work that shows a correct pivot can be valued over persevering with a flawed approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid brute force when a strategy applies (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brute force when a strategy applies (e.g., case-checking by hand when invariance immediately settles it).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalize long, mechanical case-checking when a conceptual invariant or counting argument would settle the problem; prefer conceptual clarity and economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy mismatch (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an inappropriate strategy (e.g., using induction when extremal is the right tool).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify when a chosen method is ill-fitted and leads to unnecessary complications; encourage reassessment and alternative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete induction (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to verify the base case, or using strong induction without justifying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all induction prerequisites; missing base cases or unjustified strengthening should be treated as logical flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit case omission (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming 'WLOG' when there is no symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand explicit justification for WLOG steps; omitted cases can invalidate an otherwise correct argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tight inequalities without equality conditions (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing tight inequalities but failing to state equality conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require identification of when equality occurs to demonstrate understanding and tightness of bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol-pushing without geometric/structural insight (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic manipulation in geometry problems without underlying structural reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer solutions that give geometric insight; heavy computation without explanation is a sign of incomplete understanding and should be downgraded unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended-path-or-equally-elegant-alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the solution find the intended path or an equivalently elegant alternative?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engel treats olympiad problems as deliberately constructed for a strategy; grade positively if the solver finds the intended heuristic or an alternative of comparable elegance and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-math mapping: deploy heuristics with clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: A research solution can be evaluated for whether it deploys Engel-style moves with the same recognition-and-execution clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For advanced/contextualized evaluation, check whether conserved quantities, extremal/minimal-counterexample arguments, partition/coloring analogues, etc., are used with the same rigor and conceptual transparency demanded in olympiad settings.
